comment: Plain-English headlines + summaries per motion, generated by `python -m ingest.summarize_motions` and merged into docs/data*.json by build_dataset. Keyed by a content hash of the motion (see summarize_motions.motion_key) — NOT by motion id, which renumbers. Safe to hand-edit: a corrected entry is never overwritten unless you pass --force.

001ec9fe12aed779.headline: Two Overland land items pulled for discussion
001ec9fe12aed779.summary: The council approved its routine consent agenda but pulled the SITLA land exchange and the Overland agreement out for separate discussion and votes.

010cc8116542304e.headline: Charlotte Ducos joins Community Services Board
010cc8116542304e.summary: The council appointed Charlotte Ducos to a two-year term on the Community Services Board, running April 2026 through March 2028.

03102490b6f271b6.headline: Debra Kimbrough joins Senior Advisory Board
03102490b6f271b6.summary: The council appointed Debra Kimbrough to a three-year term on the Senior Advisory Board, running April 2026 through March 2029.

04604fe5be0153f2.headline: Agreement covering the Overland area
04604fe5be0153f2.summary: The city approved a memorandum of agreement concerning Overland; the motion itself gives no detail on what the agreement covers.

05b7a0e34797dda9.headline: Approve gas power plant deal, with conditions
05b7a0e34797dda9.summary: The city approved a development agreement for a natural gas generation project, requiring simple-cycle technology, operation within five years, and trees along Pony Express Parkway.

07480df28e49ae05.headline: Pursue a justice court with Utah County
07480df28e49ae05.summary: The council added pursuing a joint justice court with Utah County to its legislative priorities list.

07aab5d2e036d00d.headline: Council to be told when concept plans reach Planning Commission
07aab5d2e036d00d.summary: The city changed its code so the council is notified every time a developer's concept plan is scheduled to go before the Planning Commission.

096d839c99c68bdf.headline: Development agreement with Flagship Homes approved
096d839c99c68bdf.summary: The city approved a development agreement with homebuilder Flagship Homes; the motion itself does not spell out the terms of the deal.

0c5f723addeb7f5c.headline: General plan updated for moderate-income housing
0c5f723addeb7f5c.summary: The council amended the general plan's moderate-income housing section, which guides how the city plans for housing that working residents can afford.

0e288f8eb26a6482.headline: Update street-connection and site plan rules
0e288f8eb26a6482.summary: The city amended its development code sections governing how new streets must connect to one another and the standards new site plans must meet.

0f5f22581bcf6ce2.headline: Tax-sharing deal for Sweetwater #4 project area
0f5f22581bcf6ce2.summary: The city agreed to collect the property taxes generated inside the Sweetwater #4 redevelopment area and hand the growth in them over to its redevelopment agency.

0f65e7bcb0db82ab.headline: Steve Conger joins Community Services Board
0f65e7bcb0db82ab.summary: The council appointed Steve Conger to a three-year term on the Community Services Board, running April 2026 through March 2029.

1157520139222e49.headline: Bryan Free joins the Planning Commission
1157520139222e49.summary: The council appointed Bryan Free to the Planning Commission, which reviews development and zoning proposals, for a one-year term through December 2026.

141fb27cfde742d2.headline: New citywide fence and screening rules
141fb27cfde742d2.summary: The city rewrote its general fencing and screening rules, changing the standards property owners must meet when putting up fences or screening walls.

14dea4e84b22e24e.headline: New rules for parking, landscaping and screening
14dea4e84b22e24e.summary: The city updated its parking and landscaping rules, requiring screening plants next to homes to be 3½ feet tall when planted and to stay green year-round.

162d6b9af76b57b2.headline: Update code sections on newspaper notices
162d6b9af76b57b2.summary: The council amended two sections of city code dealing with newspaper notices, though the motion itself gives no detail on what changed.

18b41a4ed883bdf2.headline: Sign height now measured from natural grade
18b41a4ed883bdf2.summary: The city changed its sign rules so a sign's allowed height is measured from the natural ground level, closing a loophole for signs built on raised earth.

198d0d9c3de06305.headline: Merge five city boards into one Community Services Board
198d0d9c3de06305.summary: The council took up folding the parks, sports, cemetery, veterans and economic development boards into a single Community Services Board.

19fdd9af77c0844d.headline: Push for earlier amenity-swap requests from builders
19fdd9af77c0844d.summary: The council added a proposed code change requiring amenity exchange requests to be made early in the process to its list of legislative priorities.

1bcd71f6b39c0618.headline: Set final zoning for the White Hills area
1bcd71f6b39c0618.summary: The council assigned permanent zoning to White Hills, including one commercial parcel, two farm parcels, and ten more set aside for rural agriculture.

1c188b116578f003.headline: Delay land swap with the state in Overland area
1c188b116578f003.summary: The council delayed a decision on a land exchange with the state land agency SITLA involving properties in the Overland area.

1c1f74b8b9ea84f1.headline: Approve long-range sewer plan and fee study
1c1f74b8b9ea84f1.summary: The city approved its long-range sewer plan along with the companion study that sets which future sewer projects new development helps pay for.

1edbd9d357577106.headline: First plans approved for 27-acre Spring Run Plaza
1edbd9d357577106.summary: The city signed off on early plans for a 27.35-acre development at Spring Run Parkway and Cory B. Wride Memorial Highway, starting with six lots on 8.15 acres.

23638b4d87e3cb25.headline: Rewrite of city government rules put on hold
23638b4d87e3cb25.summary: The council delayed a decision on replacing Title 2 of the city code, the section that sets out how city government is run.

2775ed0d599459dc.headline: Approve the consent agenda
2775ed0d599459dc.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, a batch of routine items passed in one vote; the individual items are not listed in the motion.

2895e8e0ec99fd85.headline: Annexation map updated, Area 1 extended to Utah Lake
2895e8e0ec99fd85.summary: The council updated the city's annexation plan, extending Area 1 to Utah Lake and requiring the map to mark old versus newly expanded boundaries and past versions.

2bfff6eede2b2165.headline: Jay Johnson joins Community Services Board
2bfff6eede2b2165.summary: The council appointed Jay Johnson to a one-year term on the Community Services Board, running April 2026 through March 2027.

2e17bbe3fdad07d1.headline: Official zoning assigned to Brandon Park area
2e17bbe3fdad07d1.summary: The city updated its zoning and future land use maps to give the Brandon Park area formal zoning designations, clarifying what can be built there.

2e85b3c3c602a517.headline: Updated design standards for shops and apartments
2e85b3c3c602a517.summary: The city adopted new design standards governing how commercial buildings and apartments must look when they are built in Eagle Mountain.

354136822e2f1afe.headline: Approve the Pacific Springs development agreement
354136822e2f1afe.summary: The city approved a development agreement for the Pacific Springs project, setting the terms the developer will have to follow.

37fb3507f124cf7f.headline: Dani McKean appointed to the Library Advisory Board
37fb3507f124cf7f.summary: The council appointed Dani McKean to a three-year term on the Library Advisory Board running from January 2026 through December 2028.

3906b550937e078f.headline: Mandy Lane appointed to the planning commission
3906b550937e078f.summary: The council appointed Mandy Lane as a planning commissioner for a one-year term covering 2026.

3f5d7595a2cbb27c.headline: Adopt Sweetwater #4 redevelopment plan
3f5d7595a2cbb27c.summary: The council made the Sweetwater #4 Community Reinvestment Area plan the city's official plan for that area and ordered the public notice state law requires.

4015c65a5ef4ad2a.headline: Third change to this year's city budget approved
4015c65a5ef4ad2a.summary: The city approved a third round of adjustments to its 2025-2026 budget, shifting spending plans before the fiscal year ends.

413db5ca042fc3c5.headline: Ivory Homes deal approved, water break dropped
413db5ca042fc3c5.summary: The city approved an agreement with Ivory Homes after weakening its pledge of developer benefits from "will" to "may" and removing a proposed cut to per-lot water requirements.

4179c6403f0edf66.headline: Second round of changes to this year's budget
4179c6403f0edf66.summary: The city amended its 2025-26 budget for the second time this year, though the motion itself does not say which amounts changed.

44fd40041700b17d.headline: Hidden Hollow amenity swap plan approved
44fd40041700b17d.summary: The city signed off on a wellness center, gym equipment and outdoor gathering area at Hidden Hollow, with the final agreement still to return for approval.

4718a702504a2186.headline: Study bitcoin as a way to pay the city
4718a702504a2186.summary: The council added studying bitcoin as a payment method for the city to its list of legislative priorities.

4b9e8c485db5c455.headline: Emily Hoehne appointed to the Library Advisory Board
4b9e8c485db5c455.summary: The council appointed Emily Hoehne to a three-year term on the Library Advisory Board running from January 2026 through December 2028.

4cd08b477b5827cf.headline: Routine items taken up in a single vote
4cd08b477b5827cf.summary: The council handled its consent agenda of routine items together, with a spelling correction to the minutes of the January 6, 2026 meeting.

51ea4965b8e28a32.headline: Notice of a proposed property tax increase
51ea4965b8e28a32.summary: The council took up a formal notice that it intends to raise property tax revenue and hold a required public hearing before any increase takes effect.

532ed6460234c068.headline: Delay changes to the city's fence rules
532ed6460234c068.summary: The council put off changes to the city's fencing rules and sent them back for more discussion at a future work session.

54e5838afc15ab7b.headline: Adopt a citywide water conservation plan
54e5838afc15ab7b.summary: The city added a Water Use and Preservation Plan to its long-range General Plan, setting official policy on how Eagle Mountain manages and conserves its water.

54f80eaa76e263d7.headline: Sell city land at $2.07 per square foot
54f80eaa76e263d7.summary: The city agreed to sell part of a city-owned parcel at $2.07 per square foot, with the buyer covering survey fees and all other costs.

556b6e9e5b47cb85.headline: Changes to the mayor's powers put on hold
556b6e9e5b47cb85.summary: The council delayed a decision on rewriting the section of city code that spells out the mayor's powers and duties.

55974898ac3a2e40.headline: Elizabeth Evans joins Community Services Board
55974898ac3a2e40.summary: The council appointed Elizabeth Evans to the Community Services Board for a one-year term running from April 2026 to March 2027.

560b169a35ad1ebf.headline: Consent agenda passed, one item pulled
560b169a35ad1ebf.summary: The council approved its routine consent items, pulled item 13.A for a later meeting, and corrected the December 16 minutes to show a 3:0 vote.

575120e5b37a1133.headline: Update rules for building on steep slopes
575120e5b37a1133.summary: The council rewrote four sections of city code covering slope development, the rules for building on hillside land, and fixed a typo.

5c7179c232e1bd11.headline: Delay changes to Overland development deal
5c7179c232e1bd11.summary: The council postponed a fifth amendment to the Overland master development agreement and will take it up at a future meeting.

5d49dfe012c02128.headline: Tax impact figures for the proposed increase accepted
5d49dfe012c02128.summary: The city acknowledged the budget officer's statement on the proposed property tax increase and the schedule showing how it would affect property owners.

5fc15cb5f1f35b35.headline: Hidden Hollow amenity swap put on hold
5fc15cb5f1f35b35.summary: The council set aside a proposed change to the Hidden Hollow site plan that would swap out planned amenities, delaying any decision to a later date.

6122b537a87857d2.headline: Jason Allen joins the Planning Commission
6122b537a87857d2.summary: The council appointed Jason Allen to the Planning Commission, which reviews development and zoning proposals, for a three-year term through December 2028.

6777498a8c4a84b0.headline: No action on rejecting the fence rules
6777498a8c4a84b0.summary: A proposal to reject the fencing code changes outright was raised but never taken up, so no decision was made on it.

6a82f26c55489d7a.headline: Changes to home-building rules rejected
6a82f26c55489d7a.summary: The council rejected proposed changes to the city's definitions and residential development standards, leaving the existing rules for home building unchanged.

6b2b79b9c30c7af2.headline: Routine items approved in a single vote
6b2b79b9c30c7af2.summary: The council approved its consent agenda of routine items in one vote, with changes to one item that had been discussed earlier in the work session.

6e456e4d7c5e00b5.headline: Routine items approved, with trails added
6e456e4d7c5e00b5.summary: The council approved its batch of routine items, adding trails to the scope of review in one of them before signing off.

701617d8c9b98d88.headline: Adopt a wildfire-risk map for homes near open land
701617d8c9b98d88.summary: The city adopted an official map of its wildland-urban interface, the areas where homes sit next to open, wildfire-prone land, and updated the related code.

705a43342717c003.headline: December 2025 named Utah PTA Centennial Celebration Month
705a43342717c003.summary: The city proclaimed December 2025 as Utah PTA Centennial Celebration Month, marking 100 years of the parent-teacher association in Utah.

734dfd285cc9605e.headline: New recreation, arts, and parks tax created
734dfd285cc9605e.summary: The city created a new Recreation, Arts, and Park Tax in its code, adding a dedicated funding source for recreation, arts, and park purposes.

7a165bf8fcb02408.headline: Overland development deal amended, with shorter lights
7a165bf8fcb02408.summary: The city approved changes to the Overland development, but required 25-foot light poles instead of 30 and completion of a 35-acre land swap with the state for a bypass road.

7f0c6df5efdcea0a.headline: ShaRee Curtis joins Community Services Board
7f0c6df5efdcea0a.summary: The council appointed ShaRee Curtis to a two-year term on the Community Services Board, running April 2026 through March 2028.

807b264076c36dee.headline: Marian Burningham joins Community Services Board
807b264076c36dee.summary: The council appointed Marian Burningham to the Community Services Board for a three-year term running from April 2026 to March 2029.

843d1280437f391d.headline: Parks master plan adopted, Sweetwater Park added
843d1280437f391d.summary: The city adopted its long-range plan for parks, trails and open space, and added the cost of Sweetwater Park to the projects funded by impact fees.

884b312d354f5469.headline: New rules for building on slopes put on hold
884b312d354f5469.summary: The council delayed a decision on changing the city's rules for development on slopes.

8911703b3b2ae71b.headline: Development deal set for Spring Run Plaza
8911703b3b2ae71b.summary: The city approved the master agreement governing Spring Run Plaza, capping required landscaping strips at 10 feet and allowing engineered retaining walls over 6 feet without tiering.

8a6b740387bed2d3.headline: Hire consultant to study Eagle's Landing market
8a6b740387bed2d3.summary: The city hired Economic & Planning Systems for a one-to-three-month market study of Eagle's Landing, a large commercial project planned along Pony Express Parkway.

8aaadeedeeeb1a16.headline: Three routine items approved on their own
8aaadeedeeeb1a16.summary: The council separately approved three routine items, numbered 10.A, 10.B and 12.A, that had been pulled out of the batch for their own vote.

8d133968ed8a08d2.headline: Public comment moved later in the meeting
8d133968ed8a08d2.summary: The council pushed its public comment period to later in the same meeting.

90a1c2083f51a27d.headline: Create a Senior Citizens Advisory Board
90a1c2083f51a27d.summary: The city created a Senior Citizens Advisory Board, giving older residents a standing group in city government.

933ecc894562afd9.headline: Chad Decoursey fills Planning Commission vacancy
933ecc894562afd9.summary: The council appointed Chad Decoursey to a vacated Planning Commission seat for a one-year term running from May 2026 through March 2027.

94d77853e78b1388.headline: November 2025 named Hunger Awareness Month
94d77853e78b1388.summary: The council declared November 2025 Hunger Awareness Month in Eagle Mountain.

97d87823c9cde42c.headline: Approve routine items, pull two for later
97d87823c9cde42c.summary: The council approved its batch of routine business but pulled the road-closure ordinance out for full discussion and dropped another item from the agenda entirely.

988a3cbedcd369fc.headline: Chad Decoursey joins planning commission as alternate
988a3cbedcd369fc.summary: The council appointed Chad Decoursey as an alternate on the planning commission for a three-year term running through December 2028.

9a73c651d5e27bfb.headline: Approve site plan for Firefly area 9.A
9a73c651d5e27bfb.summary: The city approved the master site plan for a section of the Firefly development known as NPA 9.A; no further details were given.

9bd684a3c75fc825.headline: Study speed bumps and speed tables
9bd684a3c75fc825.summary: The council added evaluating speed bumps and speed tables to its Legislative Priorities List, flagging traffic calming as an issue the city will take up.

9d24930397b4852d.headline: Support America250 and a local Utah250 committee
9d24930397b4852d.summary: The city backed the America250 Utah effort and formally recognized an Eagle Mountain Utah250 community committee.

9d45f0489af82101.headline: Tighter rules for road closures and construction
9d45f0489af82101.summary: Crews working in city streets must now file a traffic-control and resident-notification plan at least seven days ahead, get a permit, and notify the city engineer three business days before starting.

9da657a0a578c38f.headline: Consent agenda approved, one item held back
9da657a0a578c38f.summary: The council approved the routine consent agenda, but set aside item 10.A. for a later decision.

9ea6ef667575e4a9.headline: Approve the consent agenda, minus two items
9ea6ef667575e4a9.summary: The council approved its routine consent agenda in one vote but pulled two items out to be discussed separately later in the meeting.

a03274ba9d9098a6.headline: Marcia Vasquez considered for library board
a03274ba9d9098a6.summary: The council took up the appointment of Marcia Vasquez as a library board advisor for a three-year term through December 2028.

a1b98064873923a3.headline: Change fees for site plan amendments
a1b98064873923a3.summary: The council updated the city's fee schedule for site plan amendments; the motion does not state the new amounts.

a42fb0ae6cd5dec3.headline: Lacie Messerly named city recorder
a42fb0ae6cd5dec3.summary: The council appointed Lacie Messerly to serve as Eagle Mountain's city recorder.

a5a48ae00479ee2e.headline: Certify 2025 election results and RAP tax
a5a48ae00479ee2e.summary: The council certified the November 4 election, declaring Jared R. Gray mayor, Brett L. Wright and Craig Whiting councilmembers, and confirming voters approved the RAP tax.

a63c4185b40e9de3.headline: Routine consent items approved with two changes
a63c4185b40e9de3.summary: The council approved its batch of routine items, correcting a date to 2026-2027 on one and pulling another out for separate discussion later in the meeting.

a7744473c3e867db.headline: Melissa Clark named mayor pro tempore
a7744473c3e867db.summary: The council named Councilmember Melissa Clark as mayor pro tempore, the member who steps in to lead when the mayor is unavailable.

aa4d9e1b4696f758.headline: Rezone land known as QTS-SCL 2
aa4d9e1b4696f758.summary: The city approved a zoning change for the property known as QTS-SCL 2; the motion does not state the acreage or the new zone.

ae31f3e2e7e8c582.headline: Rewrite the rules for the city's Youth Council
ae31f3e2e7e8c582.summary: The council updated the section of city code that governs the Youth Council, including revisions worked out earlier in the same meeting.

afe724f7d5fcaf5e.headline: New rules for keeping animals on residential lots
afe724f7d5fcaf5e.summary: The city set standards for alternative animal management plans, with permission tied to the applicant so it ends automatically when the property is sold.

b010fc762d6bd6e5.headline: New sign rules for data centers
b010fc762d6bd6e5.summary: The city changed its sign rules to cover directional signs for data centers and other large-scale development projects.

ba151c1cad32d50a.headline: Mayor's powers held until after public comment
ba151c1cad32d50a.summary: The council set aside the rewrite of the mayor's powers and duties until later in the same meeting, so it could hear public comment first.

ba8390ec229dbea0.headline: Move to delay city land decision withdrawn
ba8390ec229dbea0.summary: A proposal to delay the decision on parcel #46:536:0430 and have the applicant seek a better solution with neighbors and city staff was withdrawn.

bccbcc538a26dafa.headline: Spring Run Plaza development approved
bccbcc538a26dafa.summary: The council approved the master development plan and zoning change for Spring Run Plaza, with the land under Roads A and B zoned Agriculture.

beefc035773e3fc5.headline: Longer construction hours for the QTS - SLC1 site
beefc035773e3fc5.summary: The council considered letting the QTS SLC1 construction site work outside the hours city code normally allows, an exception the code permits the council to grant.

bf9a3fe469ba8bb6.headline: Sell city land at $2.07 per square foot
bf9a3fe469ba8bb6.summary: The city agreed to sell part of a city-owned parcel at $2.07 per square foot, with the total set by survey and existing utility easements kept in place.

c1ebf1e2b1a5c776.headline: Consent items passed with changes to sponsorship and youth council rules
c1ebf1e2b1a5c776.summary: The city approved a batch of routine items after narrowing how sponsorship money can be spent, updating the fee schedule, and setting a five-member quorum for the Youth City Council.

c4510347c14c776c.headline: Sale of city land parcel rejected
c4510347c14c776c.summary: The council turned down a proposal to dispose of part of a city-owned parcel (#46:536:0430), land the city classifies as significant real property.

c470bac794255243.headline: Add temporary business signs to priorities list
c470bac794255243.summary: The council put temporary business signage on its legislative priorities list and asked staff to come back with a proposal for the rules.

c5a5d089d8c23823.headline: Josh Biagio appointed to the Library Advisory Board
c5a5d089d8c23823.summary: The council appointed Josh Biagio to a three-year term on the Library Advisory Board running from January 2026 through December 2028.

cbbf7bad913e0758.headline: Consent items, plus charter school intersection terms
cbbf7bad913e0758.summary: The council passed its routine consent items and attached staff conditions requiring intersection improvements for the John Hancock Charter School west campus.

cd7f19a7f28a7115.headline: Screening rules for apartment buildings delayed
cd7f19a7f28a7115.summary: The council delayed new rules on screening heat pumps and equipment at apartment buildings, asking for revisions to spacing and airflow standards before the rules return.

ce234a07251ede47.headline: Concrete form pricing added to legislative to-do list
ce234a07251ede47.summary: The council added the pricing of concrete forms to its list of legislative priorities for staff to take up.

cfb2c650bc0473a5.headline: Consent items approved; mortgage aid contract capped at 100 loans
cfb2c650bc0473a5.summary: The council approved its routine consent items, pulling the credit card policy for later and requiring the mortgage assistance contract to return if loan applications top 100.

cfdb11c54689274c.headline: Land swap with the state in the Overland area
cfdb11c54689274c.summary: The city agreed to trade properties with the state land agency SITLA in the Overland area, on the condition SITLA guarantees clean title.

d0aeca50b71295f6.headline: Delay new rules for alternative energy projects
d0aeca50b71295f6.summary: The council put off a decision on a new zoning chapter that would create an overlay zone for alternative energy projects.

d3248c1d81e909c6.headline: Susan Allen appointed Senior Advisor
d3248c1d81e909c6.summary: The council signed off on appointing Susan Allen as Senior Advisor for a three-year term running January 2026 through December 2028.

d420c4bcf28a2417.headline: Pledge city sales tax to redevelopment bonds
d420c4bcf28a2417.summary: The council took up pledging part of the city's sales and use tax revenue to help repay bonds the Redevelopment Agency plans to issue in 2026.

d61cfe930fa6a402.headline: Routine items approved, with several pulled aside
d61cfe930fa6a402.summary: The council approved its batch of routine items after setting three aside for separate votes, moving one to full discussion, and correcting spelling in another.

d79e0336ab37cba8.headline: Employee credit card policy sent back for review
d79e0336ab37cba8.summary: The council delayed a decision on changes to the city's employee credit card policy and asked staff to bring it back to a future work session.

d832e11d06d2a6ed.headline: Bid to reject Hidden Hollow amenity swap
d832e11d06d2a6ed.summary: The council weighed flatly rejecting the Hidden Hollow amenity exchange site plan change rather than leaving it tabled for a later look.

deb37438d3401890.headline: Draft 2026-27 budget accepted, hearings set
deb37438d3401890.summary: The city accepted its tentative budget for fiscal year 2026-2027 and set public hearings for June 16 and August 18, 2026, before final adoption.

dfa6b60515fc7bbb.headline: Interim 2026-27 budget and tax rate adopted
dfa6b60515fc7bbb.summary: The city adopted a temporary budget for the fiscal year starting July 2026, set the proposed certified tax rate, and dropped its DebtBook subscription.

e3e32b14f5fa2ec5.headline: Put Walmart-area sidewalk on priorities list
e3e32b14f5fa2ec5.summary: The council added money for a new sidewalk on SR-73 and Spring Run near Walmart to its list of legislative priorities.

e6121ee0b6b74fcb.headline: Water rights policy added to legislative to-do list
e6121ee0b6b74fcb.summary: The council directed staff to work with it on a policy covering paper water rights and prioritization dates, adding the task to the city's legislative priorities.

e88db35210118ecb.headline: Board terms shift to an April-March year
e88db35210118ecb.summary: The city changed when library and other board appointments run, moving terms from January through December to April through March.

e8a7409ac69f7fc7.headline: Borrow up to $230M for water and sewer work
e8a7409ac69f7fc7.summary: The city authorized issuing up to $230 million in water and sewer bonds, debt that would be paid back out of water and sewer revenue.

e9b96549abc6dcf6.headline: New rules for weathering-steel fences
e9b96549abc6dcf6.summary: The city tightened fence rules, requiring weathering steel be at least 1/8 inch thick, banning corrugated panels, and dropping an annual sealing requirement.

ed21c804323e671e.headline: Laura Jensen named Planning Commission alternate
ed21c804323e671e.summary: The council appointed Laura Jensen as an alternate on the Planning Commission for a three-year term running from May 2026 through March 2029.

eeae61b2ad0e4c58.headline: Routine items approved together on the consent agenda
eeae61b2ad0e4c58.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, a bundle of routine items passed in a single vote; the record does not list which items were included.

efbacf0276cd6a16.headline: Parks and trails master plan put on hold
efbacf0276cd6a16.summary: The council delayed adopting the parks, trails and open space master plan, sending it back to the consultant for revisions before a future vote.

f10518dcbb90547f.headline: Brent Strong joins the Planning Commission
f10518dcbb90547f.summary: The council appointed Brent Strong to the Planning Commission, which reviews development and zoning proposals, for a three-year term through December 2028.

f8c69fd69739e785.headline: Routine items passed in one batch
f8c69fd69739e785.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, the bundle of routine items handled together in a single vote.

faaef005a15d917b.headline: Noise limits now lift at 7 a.m., not 9 a.m.
faaef005a15d917b.summary: The city revised its noise rules, adjusting maximum decibel levels and moving the morning end of restricted hours from 9 a.m. to 7 a.m., seven days a week.

fb2af29e7a3b9cc1.headline: Jessie Southworth joins Community Services Board
fb2af29e7a3b9cc1.summary: The council appointed Jessie Southworth to a three-year term on the Community Services Board, running April 2026 through March 2029.
